reviews.reason: Both procedural application and exclusive-ground requirements are explicit; AND treatment is supported.

reviews.reason: Written landlord consent is expressly required; absence of it combines with the other clause (b) requirements.

reviews.reason: This is an adopted case-specific application finding concerning the amalgamation transfer.

reviews.quote:
The order of amalgamation has
been  made  on  the  basis  of  the  petition  made  by  the
transferor company  in Company Petition No. 4 of 1968 by the
High Court of Bombay. As such it cannot be said that this is
an involuntary  transfer effected  by order  of  the  court.
reviews.reason: The court expressly uses the transferor's petition as its reason for rejecting the involuntary-transfer characterization.

reviews.quote:
There is undoubtedly no written
permission or  consent of  the respondent  landlord to  this
transfer of  tenancy right  of the  1st appellant company as
required under  S. 10(ii)(a)  of the said Act.
reviews.reason: Direct adopted finding of absent written landlord consent under section 10(ii)(a).

reviews.quote:
There  is no  express provision in the said Act that in
case of  any involuntary transfer or transfer of the tenancy
right by  virtue of  a scheme  of amalgamation sanctioned by
the court  by its  order  under  ss.  391  and  394  of  the
Companies Act as in the present case, such transfer will not
come within  the purview of S. 10(ii)(a) of the said Act.
reviews.reason: The source expressly rejects an express statutory immunity for the described court-sanctioned amalgamation transfer.

reviews.quote:
the transferee company who has been put in possession of the
tenanted premises by the transferor tenant General Radio and
Appliance Co.  (P) Ltd.  cannot be deemed to be tenant under
this Act  on the  mere plea that the tenancy right including
the leasehold interest in the tenanted premises have come to
be transferred  and vested  in the transferee company on the
basis of  the order  made under  ss.  391  and  394  of the
Companies Act.
reviews.reason: Accurately preserves the court's statutory-tenant conclusion and its limited amalgamation context.

reviews.quote:
this Court held that the amplitude of S. 14(b) of the
Delhi Rent  Control Act  was wide enough not only to include
any sublease  but even  an assignment  or any  other mode by
which possession of the tenanted premises is parted.
reviews.reason: Accurately reports the earlier Supreme Court holding; the alternatives support OR treatment. This remains a reported precedent passage rather than the independently supplied Parasaram opinion.

reviews.quote:
In view
of the  wide amplitude of s. 14(b), it does not exclude even
an involuntary sale.
reviews.reason: Exact reported proposition concerning involuntary sale, subject to the supplied precedent-reporting scope.
